claims.statement: Viewer3D caps Ember's orbit distance at 25 metres.

The Columnar Furnace rises from an offset breached caldera whose collapsed terraces, open travel saddle, embedded stage crust, and through-frame lava channel establish continuous foreground, midground, and far terrain outside the protected 4.5 m action radius.
Blue-black basalt and rough obsidian dominate the frame; orange is confined to fissures and the banked, crusted river, with restrained mineral ochre as a secondary accent.
Fresh Rift uses young lava crust as Ember's surface base, exposes fractured basalt on scarps, shelters ash in depressions, and confines iron-rich alteration to lava-distance contact zones.

exemptions.name: vertical-section
exemptions.rationale: Ember is an orbit backdrop with no traversable vertical route; the four-camera composition board proves vertical scale for this gate.

exemptions.name: route-storyboard
exemptions.rationale: Viewer3D supplies a free orbit rather than a player navigation route; the locked camera board covers the intended visual sequence.

exemptions.name: walkability
exemptions.rationale: Ember is not a walkable museum room; performer action clearance and orbit sightlines are the relevant spatial checks.

exemptions.name: graybox-glb
exemptions.rationale: The Blender topology comparison was the review artifact; runtime GLB proof is deliberately reserved for the approved production-slice gate.

exemptions.name: first-person-walk
exemptions.rationale: Viewer3D is evaluated by orbit cameras rather than first-person navigation; the four-camera contact sheet is the equivalent review proof.

exemptions.name: route-duration
exemptions.rationale: There is no authored player route in an orbit backdrop.

exemptions.name: sequence-parity
exemptions.rationale: This environment slice does not select or modify any TKA sequence.

exemptions.name: state-persistence
exemptions.rationale: Ember is a stateless Viewer3D environment. It introduces no room-owned interaction state to save or restore; performer and playback state remain owned by the shared viewer.

exemptions.name: typecheck
exemptions.rationale: The repository-wide check is baseline-red outside Ember. Gate 6 records all 455 errors and 29 warnings, confirms zero EmberScene or ObsidianPlatform diagnostics, and identifies the two Viewer3D diagnostics as the pre-existing Threlte layers typing mismatch rather than stage-sizing behavior.

regressions.reason: The adversarial review found that technical acceptance did not meet the approved gorgeous-scene art bar. Hero geometry, material separation, atmosphere, and all-angle composition require new registered 3D visual targets.

Gate 4 runtime review showed every performer facing backstage. The shared Viewer3D same-direction formation heading disagreed with its negative-Z audience camera, and cast changes restored the wrong heading.

The adversarial Gate 4 review found an organ-pipe silhouette, neon-zipper fissure, procedural horizontal texture bands, interface-like emissive lozenges, and weak rear-orbit coordination. Revision 4 keeps the same capability owner and rebuilds its art language around geological mass, negative space, occluded heat, and a complete coordinated orbit.
preserved: existing runtime asset and readiness owners

regressions.reason: R6 solved environmental continuity but still read as procedural graybox geology. R7 preserves that continuous spatial chassis and replaces the focal geological language with three audited Meshy multiview modules.
preserved: R6 continuous 380 by 335 m volcanic country

regressions.reason: R7 and the Blackglass atmosphere fixed focal geology and color separation, but the broad uniform basin and 23 m flat moat still made the stage read as a contained vignette. R8 compares three registered terrain topologies and advances the strongest world-scale composition.
preserved: four unique R7 Meshy geological landmarks

regressions.reason: R8 solved the terrain silhouette and shelf-to-world continuity, but one weathered-basalt texture triplet still skins the columnar hero and all three depth bands. R9 compares three camera-registered surface ecosystems and one director synthesis before changing the production material owner.
preserved: four unique R7 Meshy geological landmarks
